# block-components

Specification: [SC-150](../../spec/normative/) &middot; 
Ledger: [`spec/coverage/block-components.yaml`](../../spec/coverage/block-components.yaml)

| Feature | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `minecraft:collision_box` | partial | Light occlusion still treats the block as a full cube: a block with a smaller collision box shadows as if it filled its space. That matches how the block is currently DRAWN — every bound block is a unit cube until minecraft:geometry lands — and moving occlusion first would give a block that is visibly a cube and shadows like a slab, which is harder to recognise than the present state. Revisit with geometry, not before. The 1.875-block cap and the requirement that the origin start inside the block are applied by truncation, and neither has been observed on a real Bedrock client; what Bedrock does with a larger box (truncate it, or refuse the block) is unverified. Truncating keeps the block, which is the outcome constitution rule 5 asks for. |
| `minecraft:selection_box` | partial | As minecraft:collision_box, which this shares its reading with. The two are resolved independently — Minecraft falls the collision shape back to the outline shape by default, and sharing one answer would make `"selection_box": false` delete a block's collision as well. |
| `minecraft:geometry` | partial | Path A only (SC-150 section 5.1): a model becomes a Java block model when every bone rotation is a quarter turn about one axis (inherited turns compose along the parent chain) and every cube rotation is one Java can express, which is one axis at -45, -22.5, 22.5 or 45 degrees. Anything else — a free bone rotation, a two-axis turn, a poly mesh, Molang bone_visibility or binding — draws as a plain cube with the block's texture and reports SCE-2031. The block is placeable, breakable and visible in every case; it is the SHAPE that degrades, never the block. A geometry no enabled pack declares is the same fallback with SCE-2030. The Z axis is mirrored on the way to Java and this IS observed — the same block was placed in both editions side by side. Everything is computed in Bedrock's space and converted once, so north and south trade places and no face is flipped or spun. The DIRECTION of a quarter turn is observed too, and it was wrong until it was: a Bedrock angle turns the opposite way round to a right-handed turn about the same axis. A block orienting one geometry through four permutations at 0, 90, 180 and -90 degrees came out with its east and west placements holding each other's rotation while north and south were right, which is the only symptom a wrong sense can have — a half turn is the same either way. Faces carry no cullface, so a face that could have been hidden by a neighbour is drawn. That costs a quad and cannot produce a hole; the reverse can. Two things SC-150 section 5.3.1 and 5.3.2 added after a real trophy came out wrong in one client and right in another. NEITHER is a fix, and both say so: A CUBE WITH NO THICKNESS on an axis emits both faces. A rule dropping one of them was written, shipped and reverted, and the reason it was reverted is the reason this note is worded the way it is. That rule was justified by a report that a real trophy's halo disappeared from the world; the reporter later withdrew it - the halo never disappeared - and the August-versus-October comparison behind it was not a comparison of Lepus at all, since the August instance ran under VulkanMod, EMF, ETF, entityculling and Figura with two resource packs loaded. So §5.3.1 does not claim what Minecraft's block model baker does with a degenerate element, because nobody has watched it. Both faces are emitted because that is the cheap answer under stated ignorance: at most one extra quad per degenerate axis, 14 of them across the 18 models Path A accepts, and 420 degenerate cubes in the surveyed packs make this the most common shape in the corpus. The attachable path is the opposite and is not a copy of this one: it builds its own quads with culling off (`entityCutoutNoCull`), so two coplanar quads really are submitted there and one has to go. A BOX UV OUTSIDE THE TEXTURE is emitted as it stands, and that half is NOT fixed. Java reads uv as 0-16 across its own sprite, so 25 faces of 1230 sample off it — 11 at u<0, 10 at u>16, 6 at v>16. Bedrock treats a negative uv origin as a wrap, and a real block model uses one. What Bedrock does where the box CROSSES the seam is not observed, so the replacement for the current output is a measured question rather than a rule, and this field stays missing rather than being written as one. |
| `minecraft:unit_cube` | partial | A block with no geometry, one naming minecraft:geometry.full_block, and one whose geometry cannot be transpiled all draw the same unit cube. The first two are exact; the third is SC-150 section 5.2's fallback and is a wrong shape rather than a wrong block. |
| `minecraft:transformation` | stub | Rotation, scale and translation applied to the model. Applied at bake for Path A. |
| `minecraft:material_instances` | partial | Only the texture is read into a MODEL, and the layer is a separate thing from the model: a bound block remembers which layer it asked for and a client installs it. Before this, a block declaring alpha_test or blend was opaque, because every block drew on the pipeline a plain block gets. A face naming an instance the block does not declare falls back to `*` rather than losing its texture, which is one typo costing nothing. THE CAUSE WAS ESTABLISHED after being chased into the wrong subsystem twice, and it is worth having in one place because the symptom is a PICTURE and not a hole. `render_method` occurred zero times in the renderer. A real trophy declares `"render_method": "alpha_test"` and ships an RGBA texture, and alpha is discarded by a shader DEFINE and not by the shader: both `terrain.fsh` and `block.fsh` gate `discard` on `#ifdef ALPHA_CUTOUT`. In 1.21.11 `CoreShaders` builds `pipeline/solid_block` with no such define and a separate `pipeline/cutout_block` with `ALPHA_CUTOUT = 0.5f`, so a transparent halo rendered as an opaque one - the shape was still recognisable, which is why it read as a corrupt texture rather than a missing block, while the same block held in the hand was correct because that path runs on `entity_cutout_no_cull`. Geometry and UV were both ruled out on the way, and the geometry rule in this same file had been written against a symptom its reporter later withdrew. **OBSERVED FIXED, on 1.21.11, on BOTH loaders, with a real trophy placed in a world.** The halo draws with its transparent pixels showing - on Fabric through `BlockRenderLayerMap.putBlock`, and on NeoForge through a mixin that took two attempts to get past a client. That is the only claim here backed by a frame, and it is why the field is `partial` rather than `ok` - `ok` would also be a claim about the three cases below, and it is not a claim about any of them. NOT FIXED, and each is a way this claim would be wrong: - **a client connected to a dedicated server.** Binding runs from `onServerStarting`, so   the client computes an EMPTY layer set and draws every transparent block on SOLID. The   same gap `WorldActivation.known()` records; SC-270 handshake closes it. - **26.2 takes the layer from the PIXELS, not from the declaration.** `FaceBakery` passes   the quad own UV rectangle to `SpriteContents.computeTransparency`, which scans the   sprite alpha inside it, and `ChunkSectionLayer.byTransparency` maps transparent pixels to   CUTOUT. An `alpha_test` block there is PREDICTED to be correct already, and what 26.2   gets WRONG is the reverse: a block declaring `opaque` whose texture contains alpha is   drawn on CUTOUT anyway. UNOBSERVED - no report about this halo has come from a 26.2 client. - **`alpha_test_single_sided` and `double_sided` are folded** into CUTOUT and SOLID.   1.21.11 has three chunk layers and both methods ask for a fourth. The IR names them   before folding so the divergence is here rather than lost at parse time.  THE PARSER IS PINNED BY `block/render_method`, including the disagreement case: an instance that declares nothing counts as opaque rather than as absent, because counting it as absent would let one alpha_test face promote a block whose other faces are unaccounted for. |
